title: What is known about 1RB0RE_1LC---_0RA0LD_1LC1LD_1RF0LA_1RC1RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RE_1LC---_0RA0LD_1LC1LD_1RF0LA_1RC1RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. A particle system on the background (1110)n: walls drift left and become runners at the left end, the head shuttles between the left end and the first runner, runners pass walls and merge in pairs into new walls; a halt needs three 0s in a row inside the tape, never seen in 1.2·1011 steps. Lean proves the sweep rules, the eleven one-cycle particle rules (for every gap size and every frozen tape to the right) and the only local pattern that leads to a halt; the missing piece is a closed list of the forms the frozen part of the tape can take.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (B1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: Where a halt can come from
claims.text: If the machine halts on its third step from a configuration, that configuration is one of: C with 0 under the head, 0 right, 1 two right. So a run can reach a halt only through one of these patterns, and a proof that the machine never halts only has to rule them out. The proof splits on the state and the five cells around the head.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 22,366 cells have been visited and 16,769 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.492).

claims.title: The sweeps cross the background words whole
claims.text: 7 shift rules: for every n and every surrounding tape, a sweep in the stated state crosses n copies of a background word and leaves n copies of its partner, in the stated number of steps (for example L F> (1110)^n R ⟶ L (0111)^n F> R).

claims.title: The only way to a halt
claims.text: The machine halts only when B reads a 1, and the only way there is F reading 0 0 0 1: in pairs, F reads 0 0, switches to A, and A reads 0 1.

claims.title: Same table as its twin
claims.text: 1RB1RF_0RC0LE_1RD0RF_1LB---_1LB1LE_1RA0LC is this table with the states renamed (A→C, B→D, C→B, D→E, E→F, F→A); it starts in the state this machine calls F. The two runs from blank tape are different (no common configuration at the left end in their first 300,000 steps), but they use the same sweeps, words and halting pattern, and every rule here holds there after renaming.

claims.title: Regular-language deciders tried (F11)
claims.text: None of these closes: each reaches a halting configuration in its abstraction, which says nothing about whether the machine halts. n-gram CPS (tools/c/ngramcps.c), equal widths on both sides: a halting local configuration is reached with plain up to width 18, history 1 up to width 18, history 2 up to width 16, history 3 up to width 16, LRU history up to width 14 (larger widths ran out of the 150 s or 60 million configuration budget). n-gram CPS with every cell tagged by its position mod p: fails for p = 2 up to width 16, p = 3 up to width 12, p = 4 up to width 20, p = 6 up to width 20. n-gram CPS where each side also carries the state of a small automaton that has read that side from the far end (every automaton with up to 3 states on both sides, or 4 states on one side), with position mod 1..4 and widths 4, 6, 8: no closed set without a halt in all 120 parameter sets. Run-length windows (the K nearest runs of equal macro cells on each side, run lengths kept exactly below T and mod M above): fails for all 72 parameter sets (cells of 1 to 4 bits, K = 2, 4, 6, T = 2, 4, M = 1, 2, 4). Two-automaton closed tape language by SAT (a deterministic automaton reading each side inward, n states each, CaDiCaL): no solution for n = 2..9; n = 10 not finished in 150 s.
claims.where: sweeps of 13 November 2026 (family F11); the tagged and run-length deciders are not in the repository yet

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Whether it halts comes down to whether the particles can ever put two 0-blocks (runners fused with 1-walls) side by side where the rightward state reads them. The rules of single collisions are proved; what is missing is a closed description of the frozen part of the tape (see the next claim).

claims.title: Eleven one-cycle particle rules
claims.text: In block notation (each block 1k0 written as k, Dn for n background blocks 1110): the runner steps right (4 Da 2 Db+1 ⟶ 4 Da+1 2 Db), walls left of it flip 1 ↔ 5 and drift left, the runner passes a 1-wall or a 5-wall in two cycles (through the fused blocks 0 and 4), two runners merge into a 1-wall, and the left end absorbs a wall in three cycles and emits a new runner. Each rule is one full cycle of the head, for every gap size and every tape right of the runner, which the cycle never reads.

claims.title: No three 0s in a row where the rightward state reads
claims.text: In the first 1.2·1011 steps the rightward state F never reads 0 0 0 strictly inside the tape (only on blank cells past the ends); at none of the 448,994 sweep starts of the first 109 steps does 0 0 0 occur inside the tape.

claims.title: The tape is a row of particles
claims.text: Blocks other than the background are walls (1 and 5, phase jump 2), runners (2, jump 3), and runners fused with a wall (0 and 4). The head turns at the first runner; everything right of it is frozen until a runner arrives. The rules in lean/Cycles.lean are the cycles with one particle ahead of the head across at least one background block; contacts at gap 0, the right end and the whole-tape sweeps are not stated as rules.

claims.title: A closed language for the frozen part
claims.text: Non-halting would follow from a list of the forms the frozen part can take, closed under one cycle, with no two 0-blocks side by side. Windowed closed tape languages (cells, blocks, cells plus a summary of the far side) all fail: the abstraction cannot see the one-cell shift a sweep makes, or guesses two 0-blocks side by side. Random tapes built from the observed neighbouring particle pairs do halt, so the invariant has to remember more than pairs.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. A particle system on the background (1110)^n: walls drift left and become runners at the left end, the head shuttles between the left end and the first runner, runners pass walls and merge in pairs into new walls; a halt needs three 0s in a row inside the tape, never seen in 1.2·10<sup>11</sup> steps. This page runs the real machine, explains the particles and the rules they follow, and lists what is proved.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.496). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.492).
After 109 steps the tape spans 22,366 cells (5,385 left of the start, 9,599 right), with a density of 1s of 0.75.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Sweeps that rewrite a periodic tape
html: <div class="col">

The head sweeps right and left across the tape, but not always to the ends: it turns at the first wall it meets, so sweeps of every length are nested inside one another, and the tape grows by a few cells at each end now and then (the square-root growth on both sides).

The two sweeps are simple finite-state rewritings. Leftward, D runs over 1s; at a 0 with a 1 on its left it swaps them (1 0 becomes 0 1, via C) and carries on, so every isolated 0 moves one cell left. At 0 0 it writes 0 1 and C turns right into A. Rightward, the head reads the tape two cells at a time in states F and A (E, C and B only make one-cell back-steps).

Almost the whole tape is the word 1110 repeated. A rightward sweep in F turns each 1110 into 0111 (one cell to the right) and the leftward sweep moves every 0 back one cell to the left, so the background survives a round trip unchanged (each of the two crossings is proved in Lean for every number of copies). The background comes in four phases (where its 0s sit modulo 4), and the tape is a row of domains of different phases. Between two domains is a wall: a block 1k0 with k ≠ 3. Walls with a phase jump of 2 alternate between 1 1 1 1 1 and 1 0 1 0 1 and drift left; walls with a jump of 1 (0 1 1 0) are born at the left end and run right fast; walls meet and merge. The picture below, one line per sweep start, shows it.
Each line is the tape at the start of a rightward sweep (time goes down, the left end is on the left). A digit is a cell inside a domain of that phase of 1110; # and _ are the 1s and 0s of walls.

sections.heading: The tape as a row of particles
html: Cut the tape into blocks 1k0 and write each block as its k. Almost every block is a 3, the background word 1110; a run of n of them is written (n), or . for one. The other blocks are particles:

blockparticlephase jump
1, 5a wall, in its two forms2
2a runner3
0runner fused with a 1-wall1
4runner fused with a 5-wall1
7, 9walls in contact (rare)0, 2

The leftmost block is the left gadget (4 when idle). Each cycle the head goes from the gadget to the first runner and back. Rightward (state F) it reads two cells at a time and crosses walls, flipping each one (1 ↔ 5); it turns at the first block with an odd phase jump, the first runner. Leftward (state D) it moves every 0 back one cell. So the tape is: the gadget, an active stretch of walls that flip every cycle and drift one block left every two cycles, the first runner, and a frozen stretch that nothing reads until a runner gets there: older runners at rest, the walls they left behind, and a periodic crystal of walls at the right end.

One line per sweep start (^ is the head; read 5(12) as a 5-wall followed by twelve background blocks). A runner passes a 1-wall (21 → 0 → 52), a wall reaching the left end is absorbed (45 → 41 → 6 → 2 → nothing) and a new runner is born (42), which then passes a 5-wall (25 → 4 → 1.2) while the old runner rests at 2(2):
(From the run of 1RB0RE_1LC---_0RA0LD_1LC1LD_1RF0LA_1RC1RE around step 107; its twin behaves the same way.)

Read together: walls flow left through the active stretch and are turned into runners at the left end; each new runner becomes the first one and the old one stops; when a runner catches a resting runner the two make a wall again. When the last two runners have merged the head sweeps all the way to the right end, where the crystal grows and releases more walls.

sections.heading: The one pattern that halts, and what a proof still needs
html: The machine halts only when B reads a 1, and Lean proves that the only way there is F reading 0 0 0 1 in step with its pairs. In blocks that is two 0-blocks side by side inside the stretch the head crosses. A 0-block is a runner fused with a 1-wall and lasts one cycle, so a halt needs two fused runner-walls next to each other, or a fused one resting in the frozen part right next to another when a runner arrives.
In 1.2·1011 steps the rightward state never reads 0 0 0 inside the tape, and at none of the 448,994 sweep starts of the first 109 steps is there 0 0 0 inside the tape.

What a proof needs. A closed list of the forms the frozen part can take (runners resting at every stage of passing a wall, the walls between them, the crystal, the right end), mapped into itself by one cycle, with no two 0-blocks side by side. The eleven rules cover a runner meeting one wall or one resting runner across at least one background block; the contacts at gap 0 and the right end are not listed yet.

What did not work. Closed tape languages built from windows (of cells, of blocks, or of cells plus a summary of the far side) all reach a halting configuration in their abstract runs: a sweep shifts the tape by one cell, which a window cannot see, and a summary of the far side cannot stop two 0-blocks from being guessed next to each other. Random tapes built from the neighbouring particle pairs seen in the run also halt, so the invariant has to remember more than pairs.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
